A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SafeSearch research. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support matching content across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original in-the-wild observations, evaluations across three search-agent scaffolds, defense experiments, configuration ablations and human validation of its evaluator.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds model evaluations, query-quality assessments, integrity controls, generation experiments and qualitative response comparisons.

M1.justification: V4 adds experimental extensions: two-baseline tiered filtering for harder cases in Appendix E and explicitly persuasive website generation in Appendix F. The original three-stage generation, attainability/integrity filtering, checklist evaluation and single-website injection procedure remain intact.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds a distinct query-quality assessment using HarmBench, WildChat, GAIA and SimpleQA Verified, extending represented data to malicious requests, real conversations and other information-seeking benchmarks. These datasets support query assessment rather than additional agent-safety benchmarking; the original five-risk coverage remains.

E2.justification: V4 Table 1 adds Claude-Haiku-4.5 and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 to both search-workflow and tool-calling comparisons. All previously evaluated main-table models remain, as do the Reminder and Filtering defense comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include GPT-4.1 query-quality scoring on a 0–5 scale, forced execution of exactly three tool calls for injection-round comparisons, and evaluations on 27-case and 108-case difficulty tiers. Appendix I newly applies safety scoring to existing benign-condition responses, explicitly reusing them. The main experiment's search and decoding defaults are retained.

E4.justification: V4 adds query-representativeness and integrity checks, injection-round and persuasiveness ablations, open-source test-generation and difficulty-tier comparisons, a January 2026 timestamp experiment, and five paired safe/unsafe response examples. V1's existing configuration ablations, human-evaluator validation and GPT-5 reasoning analysis are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs per test case and average their results. V4 introduces no new seed disclosure, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting practice. The 200-response human-agreement validation also retains the same counts and agreement rates.

E6.justification: All 35 retained main-table model/scaffold rows are numerically unchanged. V4 adds Claude results, including Sonnet's 4.6% tool-calling ASR, and recalculates aggregate averages; Claude runs are separately dated November 15. Substantial new results appear in Tables 4, 7, 8 and 10 and Figures 5 and 10, including the reported 0.81% average benign-condition ASR. These are additional findings, not same-setting improvements of retained models.

T1.justification: The mathematical description of queries, tool calls and mixing authentic results with one injected website is retained. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs; v4's expanded conceptual distinctions and empirical scoring rubric do not introduce formal theory.

C1.justification: The abstracts, introductions and conclusions retain the central claims: scalable simulation-based red-teaming, 300 cases spanning five risks, substantial search-agent vulnerability, and limited protection from common defenses. V4's additional experiments support existing claims about scalability and ongoing safety auditing.

C2.justification: V4 distinguishes unreliable search-result collections from intrinsically unreliable websites and explains the topical-relevance boundary in Appendices J.4–J.5. It adds interpretations of benign-condition failures, evaluator errors and generator dependence. It also describes helpfulness as perceived usefulness rather than factual accuracy, although the retained judging prompt still includes accuracy.

D1.justification: V4 supplies the new query-quality prompt, Claude API details and the forced-call implementation, and newly specifies greedy decoding for the original integrity-filtering agent. Public code/data access was already advertised in v1; v4 retains the GitHub address while removing the separate anonymous-access statement.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and Appendix A substantially expand positioning against RAG, agentic RAG and knowledge-poisoning research, discussing differences in control, attacker capabilities and mitigation. V4 adds Crest-Search as closely related work and introduces references supporting the new dataset comparisons, while removing some earlier citations, including FaithEval and Safetywashing.

P1.justification: V4 extensively rewrites the abstract and main narrative, moves detailed RAG comparisons and motivating-experiment setup into appendices, relocates dataset construction into experimental setup, and adds separate continuous-supervision and discussion sections. SafeSearch now consistently names the framework, with the benchmark described as its dataset.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns. V4 redraws framework diagrams, relocates the RAG comparison, combines the old reasoning-effort and risk-boundary illustrations, and adds multiple tables and response-example figures. Figure 8 also corrects the token-limit plot's horizontal-axis label, previously mislabeled as search-result count.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's reported vulnerabilities. Table 10 quantifies safety without injected content across the original agents, addressing an important attribution gap; the new timing, generator and difficulty experiments test whether findings depend on particular configurations. These additions improve confidence in the framework's validity and usefulness. The new helpfulness-description/prompt mismatch remains a limitation, but does not outweigh the stronger empirical support.
